books.section: Topic 9.5 Migration and Immigration, 1980 to the Present
Threat of Terrorism, Increase of Presidential Power, and Economic Crisis (2001–2016)

parts.modelAnswer: The photograph shows a tall metal fence running across the beach and out into the Pacific Ocean. People gather on the sand on both sides of the fence.
parts.prompt: Identify one thing the photograph shows about the United States-Mexico border.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for identifying one thing the photograph shows, such as the fence running into the ocean or people on both sides of it.
scoring.notEarned: Naming something the photograph does not show, or a vague answer with nothing identified, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Congress and presidents in the 1990s and 2000s pushed to harden the border as unauthorized crossings rose. Fences went up first in busy urban areas like San Diego and Tijuana to push crossings into harder terrain.
parts.prompt: Briefly explain ONE cause of the border fencing shown in the photograph.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one cause, such as rising unauthorized crossings or the policy of hardening urban border areas first.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a cause with no explanation, or describing an effect instead, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Apprehensions at the southwest border fell from over 1.6 million in 2000 to about 304,000 in 2017, but crossings shifted to remote deserts. The shift made the journey more dangerous for migrants.
parts.prompt: Briefly explain ONE effect of the border enforcement shown in the photograph.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one effect, such as the fall in apprehensions or the shift of crossings to more dangerous desert routes.
scoring.notEarned: Naming an effect with no explanation, or describing a cause instead, does not earn the point.
